region.text: the Moravian principality of Mojmír I, 30,182 km2 in Cliopatria's first shape

ledger.note: 822: the Moravians first appear in the record, paying tribute to Louis the Pious. 'The Moravian principality showed up for the first time in 822' and 'Mojmir I arose in Moravia in the 820s'; the page gives no founding date, so the state is drawn from its first attestation and Cliopatria's 814-821 years are held back.

region.text: Nitra, 'the neighbouring principality of Nitra'

ledger.note: c. 833: Mojmír I drives Pribina out of Nitra and unites it with Moravia. Mojmír expelled 'one Pribina' across the Danube and Pribina 'fled to Ratpot who administered the March of Pannonia from around 833'; 'conquered the neighbouring principality of Nitra' in the early 830s. Bowlus (Nitra page) holds that Nitra was annexed only under Svatopluk; Cliopatria keeps Nitra separate to 839. [Reviewer eu-15-a, 2026-10-25: quotation corrected: the page has Mojmír expelling 'one Pribina' and Ratpot 'from around 833', not 'Around 833, he expelled Pribina'; the Nitra page has 'In 833']

region.text: territory to the east, to the Bulgarian border: the Slanské Hills region (Kirschbaum)

ledger.note: Between 846 and c. 854: Rastislav extends Moravia east to the Bulgarian frontier. Rastislav page: 'In this period Rastislav seems to have acquired new territories in the east' and 'established a border with the First Bulgarian Empire', placed in 'the first eight years of Rastislav's reign' (846 onward); no single year is given, so 850 is the midpoint and Cliopatria's shape year. The Slanské Hills region is the Great Moravia page's (Kirschbaum, no year); the Rastislav page does not name it. Neither page names a state that lost it.

region.text: the Bohemian duchy of Bořivoj I, 'subordinated to Great Moravia'

ledger.note: c. 872: Duke Bořivoj of Bohemia is recognised by his overlord Svatopluk. 'In this era Bohemia was subordinated to Great Moravia' and Bořivoj was 'recognised as such around 872 by his overlord King Svatopluk I of Moravia'; the Duchy of Bohemia page: 'formed around 870 by Czechs as part of the Great Moravian realm'. Svatopluk page: in October 871 Louis the German sent troops 'against the Bohemians'. Region: Cliopatria's Duchy of Bohemia 896 shape (47,545 km2), not the gazetteer region 'Bohemia' (58,926 km2), which overlapped the Moravian shapes.

region.text: the Vistula land: Lesser Poland (Małopolskie, Podkarpackie and Świętokrzyskie), 116 cells, 29,336 km2, inside Cliopatria's 875 jump

ledger.note: c. 874-879: Svatopluk subjugates the Vistulans. Vistulans page: 'Probably around 874 they were subjugated by king Svatopluk I of Moravia', and a cited source has their 'annexation to the Great Moravian Empire between Ad 875-879'; the same page adds 'no conclusive evidence exists to prove this theory' and does not say when Moravian control ended (it names Boleslaus I's conquest in the 950s). Great Moravia page: expansion 'in the period beginning around 874' and a 'very powerful pagan prince settled on the Vistula' (no year); Lesser Poland doubtful. Confidence 2: the year is the page's (hedged), the land is the researcher's reading of the Vistulan territory as three Polish voivodeships; Cliopatria's single jump is the shape.

region.text: the rest of Cliopatria's 875 jump: Silesia, Lusatia and the Tisza-Subcarpathian fringe, 407 cells, 102,930 km2

ledger.note: c. 875 in Cliopatria; the page puts Silesia and Lusatia later. Great Moravia page: Silesia and Lusatia 'probably' annexed 'in the early 890s' (Bartl); Mojmir II page: 'Lusatia followed suit in 897' (when it seceded). Confidence 1: the single-year jump to 282,459 km2 is Cliopatria's and the 875 date contradicts the page for these lands; they stay in the 875-895 shapes, drawn soft, because the shapes follow Cliopatria. The land includes about 15,000 km2 at the eastern edge (Tisza, Subcarpathia) that the 896 Hungarian crossing then takes.

region.text: the March of Pannonia within East Francia, 'devastation of Pannonia east of the river Rába'

ledger.note: 882: Svatopluk's forces invade the March of Pannonia in the Wilhelminer War. 'His forces even invaded the March of Pannonia within East Francia in 882'; the war 'was to last until 884, led to the devastation of Pannonia east of the river Rába'. The Wilhelminer War page places the war 'in the March of Pannonia (later Austria)'. The pages record raids, not a change of ownership; Lower Austria is the researcher's reading of the March.

region.text: the March of Pannonia

region.text: the Bohemian duchy, taken over by Svatopluk after Bořivoj's death

ledger.note: Winter 890: the Bohemian duchy passes under Svatopluk's direct rule (see the gain below). Svatopluk page: 'They met at Omuntesperch ... during the winter of 890.' [Reviewer eu-15-a, 2026-10-25: source changed to the Svatopluk I page, which has 'during the winter of 890'; the Bořivoj page gives no 890]

region.text: the Bohemian duchy, ruled by Svatopluk 'himself'

ledger.note: Winter 890: after Arnulf's agreement Svatopluk rules Bohemia himself. Page: after Bořivoj died c. 889 'King Svatopluk concluded an agreement with the East Frankish ruler Arnulf of Carinthia and took over the rule of the Bohemian duchy himself'. Regino says Arnulf 'ceded the ducatus of the Bohemians to Svatopluk' but the quoted text names Zwentibald (Svatopluk page). [Reviewer eu-15-a, 2026-10-25: source changed to the Svatopluk I page, which has 'during the winter of 890'; the Bořivoj page gives no 890]

region.text: the Bohemian dukes who 'accepted Arnulf's suzerainty'

ledger.note: June 895: the Bohemian dukes swear fealty to Arnulf and leave the Moravian realm. 'The Bohemian dukes accepted Arnulf's suzerainty in June 895'; 'Among the conquered peoples, the Czechs were the first to withdraw in 895' (Svatopluk page). The Duchy of Bohemia page: 'swore fealty to the East Frankish king Arnulf in 895'.

region.text: the eastern Slovak lands and the upper Tisza that the Magyars' 896 shape holds: 210 cells, 53,109 km2, 19.1-23.4E, 47.5-49.5N

ledger.note: 896: the Hungarians cross the Carpathians into the eastern lands of Moravia. Cliopatria's Magyars 896 shape takes the same 210 cells from the Moravian 895 shape; the magyars dossier gains them from great-moravia in 896 (its ledger; the Hungarians page: 'In 895/896, under the leadership of Árpád, some Hungarians crossed the Carpathians and entered the Carpathian Basin'). Before the review these cells were lost to nobody here and gained from nobody there. Confidence 1: no page says the Magyars took this land from Moravia (a word search of the Hungarian conquest page for Tisza, Slovakia, Verecke and Subcarpathia finds no statement that Moravian land there was taken; it has only 'the territories east of the river Tisza'); the Great Moravia page has the east under Moravia since Rastislav (ledger 850), and the overlap is Cliopatria's geometry.

region.text: the northern and western lands of the maximal realm (Silesia, Lusatia, the Vistula land) without Bohemia and without the Magyar part: 537 cells, 135,807 km2

ledger.note: 896: the northern lands drop away after Svatopluk's death. 'Not long after his death Svatopluk's realm of Great Moravia collapsed in the midst of a power struggle between his sons and the intensifying Hungarian raids' (Svatopluk page). Mojmir II page: 'Bohemia, seceding from Great Moravia in the following year, became Arnulf's vassal' (895), 'Lusatia followed suit in 897', and 'When and whether the territory that is now southern Poland seceded from Great Moravia is unknown'; it is silent on Silesia and the Vistula land. Who took the lands is therefore not on any page (nobody); the year 896 is Cliopatria's (Lusatia 897 on the page). Confidence 1.

region.text: Nitra, the former Principality of Nitra, 106 cells, 26,807 km2, which the Moravian 898 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 898: Nitra leaves direct Moravian rule as an appanage (new state 'nitra', founded 898 with great-moravia as counterpart). Page: Nitra 'was ruled autonomously by the heir of the dynasty as an appanage'; Svatopluk II page: 'As Prince of Nitra, Svatopluk II was subordinated to Mojmír II' and he 'rebelled against Mojmír II in 898', with no year for the appanage itself. The year is Cliopatria's (its row 'Nitra' starts 898 and the Moravian shape drops the 106 cells). Until this event the land is direct Moravian land from the 833 gain.

region.text: Nitra, 'ruled as an appanage by the heir'

ledger.note: 898: Nitra becomes a separate appanage under Svatopluk's other heir, still tied to Moravia. Page: Nitra 'was ruled autonomously by the heir of the dynasty as an appanage'; the Principality of Nitra page's infobox has Nitra a 'vassal of Great Moravia (833-906/907)'. The year is Cliopatria's (its row 'Nitra' starts 898); the pages give none. The heir is Svatopluk II (Svatopluk II page: 'As Prince of Nitra, Svatopluk II was subordinated to Mojmír II'; reign 894-899 'Prince in Moravia (maybe of Nitra)'; after the Bavarians rescued him he 'returned to the Principality of Nitra in 901' and 'probably died in 906 in fights with the Hungarians'). The Great Moravia page has the Bavarians destroy the Nitra fortress in 899. The page gives no year for the appanage.

region.text: Moravia 'attacked and invaded' by the Hungarians in 900

ledger.note: 900: the Hungarian army 'attacked and invaded' Moravia. Hungarian conquest page: 'They exploited internal conflicts in Moravia'; the Annals of Grado say the Hungarians defeated the Moravians after their withdrawal from Italy. Zone: the Slovak part of the 900 shape, the 'eastern area' of the 902 page. Pages disagree: the Mojmir II page has 'in 900 the Magyars invaded Transdanubia' and 'raided Bavaria together with Mojmir's troops' (Moravia and the Magyars on one side in 900), and the Hungarian conquest page has 'no clear evidence either of the existence of Moravia as a state after 902 (Spinei)'.

region.text: the border strip Cliopatria drops between 899 and 900 (8,900 km2 on the west and south edges)

ledger.note: 900: Moravia shrinks to 20,901 km2 (Cliopatria 899 to 900). The strip (35 cells, 8,852 km2, 15.0-16.9E, 48.2-48.9N, on the west and south edges) lies wholly inside Cliopatria's East Franks 900 shape (35 of 35 cells) and none of it in the Principality of Hungary's, so the counterpart is East Francia (changed from principality-of-hungary after the review). Great Moravia page: Svatopluk II's conflict with Mojmír II 'gave King Arnulf a pretext to send his troops to Moravia in 898 and 899'; Svatopluk II page: 'Bavarian troops intervened in the winter of 898/899'; Mojmir II page: the Eastern Franks' troops sent in 898 were defeated by Mojmír, and a peace treaty with Eastern Francia followed in 901. No page records a cession of land, hence confidence 1: the geometry is Cliopatria's. east-franks (eu-07) has no matching gain in 900.

region.text: the eastern area

ledger.note: 902: the fighting ends with a Hungarian victory over Great Moravia.

region.text: 'occupied its eastern area'

ledger.note: 902: the Hungarians occupy Great Moravia's eastern area. 'In 902, the Hungarian armies, probably led by Kurszán, defeated Great Moravia and occupied its eastern area.' The page does not name the area; the Slovak part of the 900 shape is the researcher's reading. Caveat: the Slovak part of Cliopatria's 900 shape is only 7 cells (1,770 km2, 16.9-17.2E, 48.3-48.9N, beside Pressburg); the 'eastern area' of the page presumably means the Slovak lands further east, which Cliopatria no longer draws as Moravian after 896-898 (Nitra from 898).

region.text: Nitra, the appanage

ledger.note: 906/907: Nitra's tie to Moravia ends as the Hungarians take the land. Principality of Nitra page infobox: 'vassal of Great Moravia (833-906/907)', then 'Principality of Hungary (906/907-1000/1001)'.

region.text: the Czech remnant of Moravia, 79 cells, 19,979 km2 (the 902-907 keyframe)

ledger.note: c. 907: Great Moravia ends. Infobox 'Decline and fall: c. 907'; the text says the collapse 'occurred between 902 and 907' (Róna-Tas 902, Spinei 903 or 904, Spiesz 907); the Hungarian conquest page: 'sometime between 902 and 906'. The Battle of Pressburg (4-6 July 907) was fought against the Bavarians and 'no Moravian forces fought' in it. Cliopatria keeps the row to 910. Counterpart nobody for the Czech remnant (changed from principality-of-hungary after the review): Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary shapes hold 0-2 cells of it in 900, 911, 920, 930 and 950. Battle of Pressburg page: the 902 occupation of the eastern area was 'followed by Hungarian suzerainty over the rest of Moravia and Dalamancia', which is suzerainty, not direct rule (the principality-of-hungary dossier may carry a vassal_start). Mojmir II page: 'The remnants of the core territory of Great Moravia were divided between the newly established states of Bohemia and the Kingdom of Hungary' (after 907, no year); the Duchy of Bohemia page has Boleslaus I receive 'the lands of Moravia' after Lechfeld in 955 (duchy-of-bohemia ledger, from nobody). The 902 eastern loss stays with principality-of-hungary.

wars.name: Louis the German's campaign against Rastislav (855)
wars.outcome: The Frankish army 'foundered before the walls of one of Rastislav's strongholds' in 855 and withdrew; Rastislav raided the Danube estates. Great Moravia page: peace reached in 859.
wars.note: Rastislav had backed Radbod's rebellion in 853 (Great Moravia page). No territory changed hands.

wars.name: Louis the German's invasion of Moravia (864)
wars.outcome: In August 864 Louis besieged Dowina (Devín); 'Unable to escape the Frankish siege, Rastislav surrendered', gave hostages and swore a new oath of suzerainty.
wars.note: A Franco-Bulgarian alliance against Moravia was planned but Boris pulled out at the last minute (Rastislav page).

wars.name: Frankish invasions and Svatopluk's revolt (869-872)
wars.outcome: Frankish troops invaded both Moravian realms in August 869; in 870 Svatopluk seized Rastislav and handed him to Carloman; arrested in 871, Svatopluk was freed and drove out the Franks; in 872 Louis's armies were forced to withdraw. Forchheim, May 874: Svatopluk pledged fidelity and yearly tribute.
wars.note: The Svatopluk page dates the Forchheim treaty 874 but places the legates' request in 873. No border change is recorded.

wars.name: Wilhelminer War
wars.outcome: Svatopluk intervened as an ally of the Wilhelminers against the margrave Aribo; Pannonia east of the Rába was devastated. 'An actual agreement was not reached ... until late 885'; Charles the Fat received Svatopluk as his vassal at Kaumberg (no year given). The page's opening sentence gives the span 882-884; the agreement came 'late 885', and the war entry runs to 885 to match the contest_end.
wars.note: The Svatopluk page says the Bulgarians also invaded Svatopluk's realm during this war (no year).

wars.name: Arnulf's invasion of Moravia (892)
wars.outcome: 'Svatopluk, however, broke his pledges, so Arnulf decided to invade Moravia in 891'; 'Arnulf's invasion started in July 892, but he failed to defeat Svatopluk.' The Hungarian conquest page has the Hungarians come to help Arnulf in 892.

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin
wars.outcome: The Hungarians raided Pannonia in 894, 'attacked and invaded' Moravia in 900, and in 902 defeated Great Moravia and occupied its eastern area; the state ended between 902 and 907. At Pressburg (4-6 July 907) they beat a Bavarian army and made the Enns the frontier.
wars.note: Pages disagree on the date of the fall (902, 903-904, 906, 907): see the dissolve event.

certainty.note: The Great Moravia page: Moravia's borders 'cannot be exactly determined'. No treaty fixed a line (Forchheim 874 set tribute, not a frontier). The northern lands (Silesia, Lusatia, Lesser Poland) are the softest, flagged doubtful by the page; the Bohemian frontier is a vassal relation.

notes: Great Moravia dossier, eu-15-a. Start 822 is the first record of the Moravian principality (Mojmir I page); Cliopatria starts 814, so 814-821 are held back. Shape years are corrected by verdict, not by new shapes: _814 holds 822-824, _825 holds 825-832, _840 holds 833-849. Bohemia: Cliopatria draws it as direct land 860-895; the pages (Bořivoj I, Duchy of Bohemia) say vassal duchy (c. 872-889) then direct 890-895 under Svatopluk; shapes 860-889 minus Bohemia, ledger carries the vassal tint. The northern lands (Vistula, Silesia, Lusatia) rest on Cliopatria's single 875 jump; the pages call Lusatia/Silesia 'probable' for the early 890s and Lesser Poland doubtful: soft, confidence 1. Collapse: 902 eastern area occupied (Battle of Pressburg page), fall dated 902-907 by different historians, infobox c. 907; end 907, Cliopatria's 908-910 dropped. The Czech lands of Moravia 907-955 are on no page opened; they are not given to any successor (a gap). No area is given on the Great Moravia page, so no infobox comparison was possible. Pages not opened for lack of budget: Treaty of Forchheim, Methodius/Cyril, Pribina/Balaton Principality, Kocel, Lower Pannonia (outside every Cliopatria shape). Gazetteer names needed: Lusatia (region), Sorbia, Mikulčice and Devín (places). The Czech admin1 spelling in the gazetteer is 'Czech Republic'. Repair pass 2026-10-25 after the review: (1) 896 loss split, the 53,109 km2 (210 cells) of Cliopatria's Magyars 896 shape now goes to magyars (and magyars gains it from great-moravia in 896); the rest to nobody. (2) 898 split event for Nitra added. (3) 900 loss re-assigned to east-franks (35 of 35 cells inside Cliopatria's East Franks 900; none of the pages records a cession; eu-07 owes the mirror gain). (4) 907 dissolve of the Czech remnant to nobody; principality-of-hungary stays the successor of the 902 eastern area only. (5) The gazetteer region 'Bohemia' (58,926 km2) replaced by Cliopatria's Duchy of Bohemia 896 shape in the 860-889 corrections and in the 872, 890, 895 and 896 events; duchy-of-bohemia /ledger/1-2 still use the region (verdict thin, not touched in this pass) and should follow. (6) Wilhelminer War runs to 885. (7) 875 jump split into the Vistula land (Vistulans page, c2) and the rest (c1). Not explained: the 850-to-860 growth of 44 cells (11,128 km2) beside Bohemia. sources.title: Great Moravia
sources.note: Identity, rulers, capital, the 833 union with Nitra, territorial claims, wars with East Francia, the Hungarians, the fall 902-907.

sources.title: Svatopluk I of Moravia
sources.note: Conquests, Forchheim 874, the 882 invasion of the March of Pannonia, the winter 890 meeting with Arnulf, the 892 invasion, death 894.

sources.title: Mojmir I of Moravia
sources.note: 822 first mention of the Moravian principality; Pribina expelled c. 833; deposed 846.

sources.title: Rastislav of Moravia
sources.note: Early-850s expansion to the east; Frankish campaigns 855, 858, 864 (Dowina), 868; his capture in 870.

sources.title: Wilhelminer War
sources.note: The 882-884 war in the March of Pannonia; agreement late 885.

sources.title: Principality of Nitra
sources.note: Nitra before 833, Pribina's expulsion, Bowlus's view that Nitra was annexed only under Svatopluk.

sources.title: Duchy of Bohemia
sources.note: Bohemia formed c. 870 as part of the Great Moravian realm; the 895 oath to Arnulf; Moravia received after 955.

sources.title: Bořivoj I, Duke of Bohemia
sources.note: Bohemia subordinated to Great Moravia, recognised c. 872 by Svatopluk; Svatopluk took over the duchy after Bořivoj's death c. 889.

sources.title: Battle of Pressburg
sources.note: 902: Hungarian armies defeat Great Moravia and occupy its eastern area; the 4-6 July 907 battle.

sources.title: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin
sources.note: 900 attack on Moravia; the destruction of Moravia between 902 and 906; 894 Pannonia campaign.

sources.title: Mojmir II
sources.note: Bohemia seceded 895, Lusatia 897, southern Poland undated; Bavarian troops 898; peace with Eastern Francia 901; remnants divided between Bohemia and Hungary after 907.

sources.title: Svatopluk II
sources.note: Prince of Nitra under Mojmír II; rebelled 898; Bavarian intervention winter 898/899; returned to Nitra 901; died c. 906. Silent on the year of the appanage.

sources.title: Vistulans
sources.note: Probably subjugated by Svatopluk I around 874 (annexation 875-879 in a cited source); no conclusive evidence; end of Moravian control undated.
